text:
Jacob Quillan has played three games for the Canucks and already leads the team in fighting majors, as David Quadrelli of The Nation Network noted. The undrafted Quinnipiac product came up when Filip Chytil went on injured reserve, made his Canucks debut against Toronto, the team that first signed him, and has drawn praise from The Province and The Hockey Writers.

The highlight so far: a board battle that set up Brock Boeser's goal in Winnipeg, which Daniel Wagner called "a fantastic battle win." That's his one point in three games, at about 11 and a half minutes a night.

There's almost nothing to measure yet. He had 24 games with the Maple Leafs before this season, and Evolving-Hockey's read on those 236 minutes was around replacement level against tough competition. Our range for a full season runs from 3 to 12 goals, which is another way of saying a big unknown. What he's showing is energy and willingness, and on a Canucks team that has been called out for effort, that gets noticed. Whether it earns him a longer stay depends on Chytil's timeline.
headline: Quillan makes a case
